analyst_view.overall: A Breton derby between Lorient (10th, 15 points) and Rennes (8th, 16 points), one point apart. Lorient (Alexandre Dujeux) have one of the league's tightest defences, have won the last six league meetings and beat Le Havre 2-0 before the break; Katseris is out and Isaak Touré and Ibrahima Baldé are doubts, all three counted out by the numbers. Rennes have lost three of their last four and dropped from first to eighth; Franck Haise answered public criticism from chairman Nicolas de Tavernost, and top scorer Estéban Lepaul (seven goals) is back in training and a candidate for the squad after an ankle injury, while Frankowski is out (counted) and Rongier travels after a precautionary rest. The numbers do not flag this as a derby, and Marc Bollengier (4.1 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Lorient's tight defence is already in them, but Lepaul, Rennes' top scorer, is back after missing the games the numbers learned from, and Touré and Baldé are only doubts though counted out, so I lean slightly higher, to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Lorient's 3-4-2-1 and Rennes' 3-5-2 both rely on wing-backs, which the numbers already reflect, and Rennes having to break down a compact block is how this fixture usually goes, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards with Bollengier's record in, but they do not treat this as a derby. Breton derbies are usually fierce and Rennes are under pressure from their chairman after a poor run, so I add a little, to about 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Lepaul's return helps Rennes' finishing more than their number of shots, and Lorient's compact style is unchanged, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. A sharp striker like Lepaul back in the squad should put a few more efforts on target, though he may start on the bench, so I nudge it up only to about 9.2.
